trigger: The node hosting a replica has its HTTP port partitioned (SocketProxy closed) while it stays in live_nodes, so DELETEREPLICA's UNLOAD fails; during the Overseer's 30 s wait the node restarts from the same disk under a new port and re-registers the replica with the new node_name, so the fallback DELETECORE (carrying the old node_name) is ignored and the second wait times out.
reason: The triggers (HTTP partition, node restart under a new address) are realistic, but the outcome is a fail-safe, not broken coordination. The DELETECORE fallback is deliberately scoped to the node the Overseer meant to delete from: SliceMutator.removeReplica removes a replica only if its node_name matches (SliceMutator.java:131-134), which keeps a stale, node-scoped delete from removing a replica now live on another node. With the UNLOAD never delivered and the replica re-registered elsewhere, DeleteReplicaCmd honestly reports that the replica could not be removed (DeleteReplicaCmd.java:276-278). The cluster stays consistent (the replica still exists and the client is told it failed), and a retry with a fresh snapshot deletes it. This is a normal failure of an admin operation when its target node fails mid-operation, which the caller handles.
